title: Textile industry in the UK
titleCn: 英国纺织业百年变迁与就业机会

paragraphs.text: You will hear a university lecturer talking to a group of prospective students about the fashion and textiles industry in the UK.
First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.
Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text:
know you're all interested in getting a qualification in textiles, so now I'm going to look at the kind of opportunities that will be open to you.

00:01:30,500

But first of all, I'll give you a brief history of the fashion and textiles industry so you can see how the industry has changed over the last hundred years or so.

00:01:41,060

The textile industry has been historically important to the development of the UK economy. In the first half of the twentieth century, employment in the industry reached a peak at one point five million. It's now about three hundred thousand. At that time, every aspect of the business would be managed within a single company: design, manufacturers, and distribution. And many of these companies belonged to the same family for generations.

00:02:11,720

In the second half of the twentieth century, producers in other parts of the world began to compete. With the competition from abroad, many manufacturing companies had to shut down, and jobs were lost. Most of those larger clothing companies that managed to carry on closed all their facilities for production and became distributors of clothing rather than manufacturers. Nowadays, the majority of turnover in the fashion market is in clothes made for women, but men's and children's clothes are expanding, and that is likely to continue.

00:02:45,680

Over the last twenty years, there has been investment in research into textiles suitable for outdoor clothes, and these were later adapted for the fashion market. Because of this, there is less interest in traditional fabrics for fashion clothing, and this trend is likely to continue.

00:03:07,640

So let's have a look at the fashion and textile industry in the UK today in a bit more detail and at the kind of jobs that are available.

00:03:16,900

Although, as I said, the industry has declined, it is still important to the UK economy.

00:03:23,480

The difference is today that there are hardly any large companies, and most people work for businesses with between one and ten people.

00:03:32,540

The workforce is split evenly between clothing and textiles. The total value of goods produced in the clothing and textiles sector is pretty amazing still. The industry produces goods worth about sixteen point five billion pounds a year. Of that, about a third is exported.

00:03:53,020

Although there has been a reduction in total numbers employed in the industry, because of the move away from a mainly manufacturing focus, there is probably a wider scope for graduate careers than before.

00:04:05,260

It's still very competitive, though. There has always been recruitment amongst engineers, and that continues, but globalization has also opened up opportunities for those fluent in foreign languages, so those are skills you could develop.

00:04:20,500

Many of you will be looking for a design job, but in fact, less than one percent of those in the industry are employed as designers, so you need to think beyond that.

00:04:31,840

Now looking at the future of the clothing industry in the UK, many people think that the key to success will be the manufacture of traditional textiles, for example, of cloth for business suits. However, in my opinion, we are lucky enough to have creative designers who lead the world in producing the latest styles for the high street, and that will be the biggest sector for growth.

00:04:56,280

So let's look at a few jobs that you may not have thought of.

00:05:00,600

Some of you might be interested in being a textile technologist.

00:05:04,860

They are employed by fashion retailers or suppliers, and they work with the fabrics used to make clothing. They're responsible for checking on new developments in materials and sometimes producing them themselves. But they don't actually design the clothes. They leave that to the fashion designers. If you prefer to be at the other end of the production process, being an operations manager might appeal to you. They are in charge of the coordination production from fabric to finished piece of clothing. That involves making sure that the goods are produced to a schedule, so shops and their customers don't have to wait for what they need.

00:05:44,800

Many textiles graduates work in the retail sector, and there is a range of jobs there, including merchandisers and visual merchandisers, two quite different roles.

00:05:56,200

Merchandisers decide what quantities of a range of clothes or whatever to stock in individual shops, and they have control of a large budget.

00:06:05,740

Don't confuse this with the job of a visual merchandiser, whose job is to persuade the customer to buy.

00:06:12,630

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text:
visual merchandiser is responsible for the look of a store. They decide what is going to be on show, both in the window and inside the shop.

00:06:22,330

These will be changed regularly as the seasons change.

00:06:26,400

There are other jobs, so if anyone would like any further information...

00:06:32,980

That is the end of part four. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to part four.
